title: Nth Root of a Number
description:
Return the integer `k` with `k^n == m`, or `-1` when `m` is not a perfect `n`-th power.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= n <= 30`
- `1 <= m <= 10^9`
hints: Binary search `k` in `[1, m]` and compare `k^n` with `m`.
Stop multiplying as soon as the running power passes `m`, or it will overflow in some languages.
complexity: O(n log m) time, O(1) space

editorial.explanation:
The `n`-th root is monotone in the candidate, so binary search `k` in `[1, m]` and compare `k^n`
with `m`.

Computing `k^n` naively overflows fast; stop multiplying the moment the running product passes `m`,
since that already answers the comparison.

`O(n log m)` time, `O(1)` space.
editorial.complexity: O(n log m) time, O(1) space
